lines: +//! A text input that grows to fit its text: a row for each visual line, lines
+//! broken with Enter and long lines that soft wrap alike, from a single row up
+//! to a most, after which it scrolls. It shrinks as text goes, and fits again
+//! when its width changes. Whatever shows the input keeps a [`GrowToFit`],
+//! sizes the editor with [`GrowToFit::heights`], and puts
+//! [`GrowToFit::tracker`] over it, so the fit follows how the editor is laid
+/// Room the editor keeps free at the right of each line when soft wrapping.
+/// How an input is fitted to its text, from how its editor was last laid out.
+    /// Width the editor's text was last laid out in, which decides where long
+    /// What the editor adds around its rows (padding and border) as last
+    /// laid out, rounded to device pixels.
+    /// How tall the editor is for its text, and how tall a single row of it
+    /// is, for lining things up with it.
+        let rows = self.visual_rows(&text, window, cx).clamp(1, self.max_rows);
+        // Fit the text with the editor's own metrics: its laid-out line height
+        // plus the padding and border around its rows. Until the editor has
+        // painted, the border is estimated at a device pixel or more per side.
+            ceil_to_device_pixel(line_height * rows as f32 + chrome, window),
+    /// The rows `text` takes in the editor: one per line, plus one for every
+    /// soft wrap, wrapped the way the editor wraps it.
+    fn visual_rows(&self, text: &str, window: &Window, cx: &App) -> usize {
+        let Some(wrap_width) = self.text_width.map(|width| width - WRAP_RIGHT_MARGIN) else {
+    /// Laid over the editor: once the editor has painted, checks how it was
+    /// laid out, the width its text wrapped in and the padding and border
+    /// around its rows, and when either changed, has `owner`, which keeps the
+    /// fit where `fit` finds it, draw again to fit anew.
+/// `length` rounded up to a whole device pixel. The editor lays its rows out
+/// on device pixels, and rounds a height that falls between device pixels
+/// half toward zero, so at fractional scales an input sized in logical pixels
+/// can come out a fraction of a pixel short of its rows; the editor then takes
+/// its last row for out of view and scrolls it in for a frame, which flickers
+/// the text a line up and back.
+    // Float noise just past a whole device pixel must not round up to the next.

head -8 spec/ui/components/git-panel/index.pi; head -14 spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi; mkdir -p spec/ui/components/growing-text-input && cat > spec/ui/components/growing-text-input/index.pi <<'EOF'
use /lib

export scope GrowingTextInputScope:
    concept: {GrowingTextInputConcept}

concept GrowingTextInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line text input that is only as tall as its text, so it takes
        a single row until there is more to show.

    shape: {GrowingTextInputShape}

shape GrowingTextInputShape:
    description:
        A multi-line text input whose long lines soft wrap, starting at a
        single row.

    growToFit:
        It grows to fit its text, one row per visual line: both lines broken
        with <Enter> and long lines that soft wrap, wrapped where it wraps them.
        It shrinks again as text is removed, and fits again when its width
        changes, as when the window is resized. Its height is what its rows and
        their padding and border take, and nothing more: there is no empty row
        beneath the last line.

    mostRows:
        Whatever uses it says how many rows it grows to at most. Once its text
        takes more, it stays that tall and scrolls.

    steadiness:
        It grows or shrinks in the very frame its text changes, and at any
        display scale its height is rounded up to a whole device pixel, so the
        text never flickers a row up and back as a line is added.
EOF

content.text:
The commit message box in the git panel now starts at one line and grows with its text, the same way the chat input does, up to 10 lines before it scrolls. The growing behaviour is now shared code with its own spec scope. All tests pass (168, 1 ignored); I haven't looked at the git panel in the running app.

**Spec:** the new `spec/ui/components/growing-text-input/index.pi` defines `GrowingTextInputScope`. It says the box:
- starts at a single line;
- grows one line for each typed line break and each soft wrap, and shrinks as text is removed;
- fits itself again when its width changes, with no empty line below the text;
- stops growing at whatever limit the screen using it sets, then scrolls;
- has a height snapped to whole screen pixels, so it doesn't flicker as lines are added.

The chat input spec now just says it's a growing text input with a 12-line limit, lined up with the Send button. The git panel spec says the commit message is one with a 10-line limit, replacing "a few lines tall". `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly.

**Code:**
- The chat input's sizing code moved into a new `src/growing_input.rs`, and `src/chat_input.rs` now uses it with the same 12-line limit.
- `src/git_panel.rs` uses it for the commit message and drops the fixed 76px height.
- The existing chat input tests for growing, shrinking and no flicker at every display scale pass unchanged.
- A new check in the git panel's commit test confirms the message box starts at one line, is exactly two lines taller with three lines of text, and stops at 10 lines when given 30.

I picked 10 lines as the commit message limit; say if you'd like it different.
